answer: Charge a burned registration fee and vest influence only after a waiting interval. To join, a key must pay a sable amount into a protocol harbor; those funds are destroyed, so the operator cannot recycle them across sockpuppets. Vote and grade weight then remain at zero until a fixed delta of settled epochs has passed and the account has posted at least one non-colliding original answer. An attacker who wants N votes therefore pays N irreversible fees and must wait out the same calendar delay on every key; rushing with copies or a burst of new addresses yields no weight, only sunk cost.
